output:
Dear Mr Kehinde Ogunleye,

Thank you for keeping my bag safe and calling the number on my lab manual. I appreciate that you made the effort to contact me rather than discard it.

I am writing about the black Jansport bag I left in the Oshodi–Igando danfo on Friday evening, 6 November, when I came down at Ikotun. It contains my lab manual, dissecting kit, student ID card, two textbooks, calculator and glasses.

Sir, I am a first-year Biology student, and I have my BIO 101 practical on Wednesday, 11 November, at 10 a.m. Without my dissecting kit, I will not be allowed into the practical. My ID card, books and glasses are also important for my studies.

I can manage ₦10,000 towards your transport and as a sincere thank-you for keeping the bag. That is my entire allowance, and it is the most I can afford. I cannot raise ₦40,000. Please accept the ₦10,000, which I can give you when we meet and you return the bag.

You spoke kindly during our first call, so I was worried when you later said I should pay ₦40,000 or forget the bag. I am grateful for your help, but I do not think it is fair to make returning my belongings depend on a payment I cannot afford. I would like us to settle this respectfully.

Please choose a day and time before Wednesday when we can meet during daylight. My roommate, Adaeze, will accompany me. We could meet at Ikotun roundabout or, if convenient for you, outside the Ikotun Police Division gate, simply as a public meeting point. I am also happy to agree on another suitable public place around Ikotun.

Kindly reply to confirm whether you will accept this arrangement and when we can collect the bag. Thank you for your understanding.

Yours sincerely,  
[Your name]
